request_payload.input: We are comparing two English natural-language-inference classifiers. We want to know which one better tracks who did what to whom when deciding whether a hypothesis follows from a premise, including cases where the two sentences use almost the same words. Recommend a public evaluation resource and scoring plan, and state what conclusion it would justify.
request_payload.instructions: Answer the research question from existing knowledge. Aim for 180–240 words and do not exceed 300 words. Do not browse or use external tools. Do not ask a follow-up question.

output_text: Use the public Winograd Schema Challenge (WSC) split from SuperGLUE as a minimal probe for English NLI role tracking. Each WSC item contains two noun phrases and a pronoun whose correct antecedent is determined by the action’s semantics. Convert every item into two NLI pairs: premise = original pronoun sentence; hypothesis 1 = same sentence with the pronoun replaced by the gold entity, labeled entailment; hypothesis 2 = replacement by the non-gold entity, labeled contradiction. Remove malformed or lexically ambiguous items. Evaluate both classifiers on the same fixed split without tuning on it. Treat neutral as incorrect for both labels. Score overall accuracy, macro-F1 for entailment/contradiction, and a role-swap metric: the proportion of items where the classifier correctly labels both the gold replacement as entailment and the incorrect replacement as contradiction. Report 95% bootstrap confidence intervals and a paired McNemar test. Prefer the classifier with significantly higher role-swap accuracy or macro-F1, especially on high lexical-overlap items. This would justify concluding that it better tracks who performed the action and who was affected, rather than merely matching surface words; the other is more vulnerable to subject-object confusion in near-identical sentences.
capture_note: Final message/output_text preferred; delta fallback explicitly flagged and never silently completed; durable sanitized SSE journal retained
